item.title: Rubio to meet Ambani in Jamnagar: Venezuelan oil, energy on agenda
item.description: With the whole world watching, Marco Rubio will meet Mukesh Ambani today in Jamnagar, home to the world's largest oil-refining complex ...
item.dc:creator: Akshita Singh
item.content:encoded: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is all set to visit Reliance Industries’ Jamnagar refinery in Gujarat on Wednesday and meet chairman Mukesh Ambani, with energy cooperation and investment among the key issues on the agenda. Rubio, 55, is in India on a three-day official tour. On the first day of his visit, Rubio met External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar in Mumbai, where the two sides discussed trade, energy, technology, defence and people-to-people ties. Rubio said the proposed India-US trade agreement was close to finalisation, with a few issues remaining. Rubio’s meeting with Ambani comes as India and the US seek to strengthen economic and energy ties despite differences over trade tariffs, Russian oil purchases and immigration policies, with Washington pushing for greater purchases of American energy and technology by Indian companies. Here’s what’s likely to be on agenda for Rubio-Ambani meet today:Energy security and diversifying oil suppliesEnergy cooperation is expected to be a key focus of Rubio’s engagement with Reliance. On Tuesday, Rubio said in Mumbai that India has the capacity to process Venezuelan crude and that some Indian companies already held oil concessions in the South American country. Describing India as a “refining superpower”, he said the proposed discussions with Reliance would cover opportunities to increase refining and oil production. Notably, the US has long been urging India to diversify its energy sources, while New Delhi has continued to buy Russian crude despite pressure from Washington. India’s dependence on Russian oil has been a source of friction between the two countries. Russian crude accounted for about 40 per cent of India’s oil imports this year, with supplies reaching nearly 2 million barrels per day, according to Bloomberg. Rubio said India had made progress in diversifying its energy portfolio and that the US could supply some of its energy requirements. “India has expressed repeatedly its desire to diversify its energy portfolio, which is a smart thing to do. It’s not easy to do that from one day to the next,” he said. ALSO READ: Rubio meets Jaishankar in Mumbai, pushes for early India-US trade dealWill Reliance refine more Venezuelan crude?One specific issue Rubio has raised is the possibility of Reliance processing more crude oil from Venezuela. The US is looking to bring additional Venezuelan supplies to global markets amid disruptions linked to the conflict involving Iran. Reliance’s Jamnagar complex, the world’s largest refining complex, has the capacity to process heavy crude. “They also, by the way, have pre-existing oil concessions in Venezuela that can produce more themselves,” Rubio said. Rubio said the US delegation would discuss the potential for greater Venezuelan oil production and refining with Reliance. However, no agreement to expand such processing has been announced as of now. He also acknowledged that Venezuelan supplies alone could not fill all potential gaps in global oil markets, although they could help in the short term.Reliance’s US investment and wider commercial tiesReliance’s business interests in the US provide another area of potential discussion during Wednesday’s meeting. The company has partnered on a new refinery project in Brownsville, Texas, according to Bloomberg. The proposed facility adds a commercial dimension to the relationship between Reliance and the US, alongside the immediate question of energy supplies. Rubio’s visit is also part of a broader engagement with Indian business leaders, including representatives of the Adani Group and Tata Sons. The US has been seeking greater commercial investment and stronger economic ties with India.India-US trade deal and strained bilateral tiesRubio’s visit comes as New Delhi and Washington work towards finalising a bilateral trade agreement after more than a year of negotiations. The proposed pact is intended to address tariff differences, non-tariff barriers and market access. India is seeking competitive tariff terms for its exports to the US, while Washington has raised concerns about duties on American goods entering the Indian market. Speaking in Mumbai, Rubio said the two countries were close to an agreement, with a small number of issues left to resolve. He expressed hope that the deal would be finalised shortly. Bilateral relations have also faced pressure over US tariff measures, India's purchases of Russian oil and changes to American immigration policies, including higher H-1B visa fees.

item.title: SBI probes suspected dark web leak involving 3,897 customer records
item.description: SBI has flagged suspected customer data exposure on the dark web, with preliminary analysis identifying 3,897 records containing personally identifiable information.
item.dc:creator: Subrata Panda
item.content:encoded: The State Bank of India (SBI), the country’s largest lender, has flagged suspected exposure of customer data on the dark web, with a preliminary analysis identifying 3,897 customer records containing personally identifiable information (PII), according to a disclosure to the stock exchanges. The bank received alerts on October 16 from its threat intelligence service provider, the Defence Cyber Agency and the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) regarding the suspected exposure of customer data on the dark web. A preliminary analysis of around 375,000 records available on the dark web identified 3,897 customer records containing personal information. The information included registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, names, gender, email addresses, residential addresses, branch and customer information file (CIF) identifiers, lead IDs, and metadata associated with loan and lead records. SBI said a detailed investigation was required to establish the authenticity and completeness of the exposed data, determine the potential source and extent of the exposure, and assess the risks to customers and the bank. The lender activated its cyber incident response and containment protocols and engaged an independent cybersecurity agency empanelled by CERT-In to conduct a comprehensive assessment and investigate the alleged compromise. A detailed assessment is under way, and the bank said it was implementing appropriate remedial and preventive measures, as required. The bank said the incident had no material impact on its core business operations, financial performance or business continuity, adding that its core business functions continued to operate normally. “We wish to submit that this does not have any material impact on Bank’s Core business operations, financial performance or business continuity,” the bank said.

item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / Musk ordered slowdown of Starlink service used by Ukraine's military

Musk ordered slowdown of Starlink service used by Ukraine's military Ukraine uses Starlink for battlefield communications and drone operations. Restricting the satellite service hampered the country's attack and air defence drone missions against Russia

Musk and US President Donald Trump discussed the Starlink decision in a call soon after the slowdown became public (Photo: Reuters)

Reuters 2 min read Last Updated : Oct 21 2026 | 8:21 AM IST

Listen to This Article

Elon Musk last week ordered the slowdown of a military-grade version of SpaceX's Starlink satellite service that Ukraine relies on, the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday, citing US officials and people familiar with the matter.   Musk, SpaceX and the White House did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment. Reuters could not immediately verify the report.   Ukraine uses Starlink for battlefield communications and drone operations. Restricting the satellite service hampered the country's attack and air defence drone missions against Russia.   Musk and US President Donald Trump discussed the Starlink decision in a call soon after the slowdown became public, while the president was campaigning last week, according to the report, which added the two had also discussed the matter prior to the decision to throttle Starlink.

Reuters had reported exclusively that the order to limit the satellite system came from inside the White House. Also Read

Tesla shareholders to vote on Musk's re-election, $158 bn pay on Dec 3

Ukraine suspects US restricting intelligence sharing on Russian Attacks

Putin proposes summit with Trump, Xi Jinping to discuss Ukraine deal

Elon Musk says he will gift SpaceX shares to 'every kid in America'

Diesel deal aimed to keep peace talks with Russia going, says Trump

Trump said last week he did not think either he or Musk was responsible for Ukraine losing Starlink access, while Musk said any limits on speed or Starship use were decided by the US military or the president.   Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskky's relations with Washington have sunk to new lows after Trump announced a deal to buy Russian diesel and waived new sanctions on Moscow. Trump has also told Kyiv to stop attacking Russian refineries and urged Ukrainians to replace Zelenskky.   Zelenskky, who is in Oslo in a bid to repair US relations, said on Tuesday he discussed issues including "the situation with Starlink/Starshield, which needs to be restored" with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said on Tuesday Washington had not pulled back Ukraine's ability to access Starling's satellite network, but signaled the problem lay with the terms of service Kyiv needed to comply with.

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

item.title: Japan launches historic mission to collect samples from Mars moon Phobos
item.description: Japan's MMX mission will collect at least 10 grams of material from Phobos and return it to Earth by 2031, aiming to resolve how Mars' two moons formed and evolved ...
item.dc:creator: Unis Ahmad Dar
item.content:encoded: Japan has launched a $578 million mission to bring back the first samples from a Martian moon, Reuters reported, in a bid to settle how Phobos and Deimos formed. The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) launched the Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) spacecraft aboard its H3 rocket from the Tanegashima Space Centre on October 20. The spacecraft is expected to reach the Martian system in August 2027 and return samples to Earth in 2031. The mission aims to collect at least 10 grams of material from Phobos, the larger and closer of Mars’ two moons. If successful, it will become the first mission to return samples from a Martian moon, giving scientists material they can examine in laboratories on Earth. Why Phobos? Phobos offers scientists a way to investigate the Martian system without attempting the more difficult task of collecting and returning samples directly from Mars. The moon measures roughly 27 km by 22 km by 18 km and orbits about 6,000 km above Mars. Its relatively weak gravity makes landing and collecting material technically different from operating on a planet with stronger gravity. Its proximity to Mars is another advantage. Scientists believe Phobos may have accumulated debris ejected from the planet by meteorite impacts. Studying this material could provide evidence of how Mars evolved over billions of years. Phobos may also preserve clues about the composition and history of small bodies in the Solar System. Determining whether it originated from a collision involving Mars or was captured from elsewhere would help researchers understand how planetary systems formed. Beyond planetary science, MMX will test technologies needed for future missions to Mars, including surface landings, sample collection and the return of material across interplanetary distances. What will the probe do? MMX will travel for about a year before reaching the Martian system in August 2027. It will then conduct detailed observations of Phobos and study Deimos during flybys. A French-German rover, named IDEFIX, will be deployed to Phobos to examine its surface and help assess suitable landing sites. The main spacecraft is expected to land on Phobos around 2029-30 and collect samples using its sampling equipment. JAXA aims to retrieve at least 10 grams of surface material. The spacecraft will then leave the Martian system and begin its return journey, with the sample capsule expected to reach Earth in 2031. The mission is designed to last about five years. Japan has earlier sent two missions to return samples from asteroids–Hayabusa and Hayabusa2. However, travelling to the Martian system, operating in Phobos’ low-gravity environment and returning samples to Earth will pose a different challenge, scientists say.
